 (Chapter-IV) Total -  NIL 

 
CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation/Observations  
1.1 The Committee directed the Chief Engineer (NZ-1) and the Superintending 
Engineer, CPWD, who were also present, to prepare a proposal for renovation/repair of 
sports Infrastructure at NSNIS, Patiala by taking inputs from the coaches concerned and 
to see that it is as per International standards and submit to the Department of Sports for 
approval.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                            (Para 53) 
 
Action Taken 
Institute has already taken action to get the renovation/up gradation works of sports 
infrastructure executed. R
epair/renovation of following buildings have been completed:- 
i. Renovation / up gradation of Dhyan Chand Internation al Hostel. 
ii. Renovation / Up gradation of Change rooms, cum toilets &stores in different 
outdoor playfields. 
iii. Renovation & upgradation in two of the four toilet blocks in silver jubilee 
hostel for women. 
iv. R e n o v a t i o n  & up gradation of Sauna / SteamBath Comple x. 
v. Renovation & up gradation of Guest House. 
vi. Annual repairs of staff quarters. 
vii. Annual repair of Main Palace building. 
 
In addition to above, the work of renovation/up gra dation of Yadavindra Hostel & 
Sports Sciences building are under progress. 
 

 
 
CHAPTER-II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE 
DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S 
REPLY 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.1          The Committee attention was drawn t o  G y m n a s t i c s  s t u d e n t s  o f  
Hyderabad, who are taking coaching in Sports Authority of India Cent re. It was pointed 
out that recently this SAI centre including Hostel was shifted f rom Saroonagar 
Indoor Stadium, LBB Nagar to Gachibowli except sports of Gymnastics and 
Badminton. Nearly 30 students are taking coaching i n Gymnastics as day boarders and 
10 students (State and National Level medalists) are residing in S AI Hostel to 
takecoaching while continuing their studies in nearest schools at LB Nagar. It was 
informed that due to shifting of this centre to Gac hibowli, these 10 students are facing 
severe problem to attend the collage, practice, and  for mess due to lack of 
accommodation.  They had requested Regional Directo r and Deputy Director, SAT 
to facilitate them at Saroonagar Indoor Stadium for  their training, at least for this 
academic year. However, no response has been received from their end. Now these 
students are facing hardship due to lack of accommodation, as they have  to attend the 
collage for their education at Saroonagar and then to rush back to report at Gachibowli 
for their training ad practice.  They all belong to very  poor families.  It was brought to 
the notice of Committee that though these students are perusing gymnastics since 
eight years
, due to the prevailing conditions they are being forced to leave the game. It 
was, therefore, requested to help the students to s urvive in this game while 
continuing their studies.                                            (Para 30) 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.2 The Committee took serious note of this fact. The Committee feels that these 
budding sportspersons who have been pursuing the Gymnastics from the very young age 
need to be nurtured and encouraged. The Committee is surprised to note this sorry state 
of affairs in management and recommends that the respective authorities of SAI are 
required to take cognizance of the plight of budding Gymnastic sportspersons and make 
sure that these students are shifted back to the Saroornagar Indoor Stadium or should be 
provided hostel facilities at Gachibowli itself so that they pursue their studies and games 
simultaneously.             
                                                                                                                           (Para 31) 
 
Action Taken 
The Secunderabad Centre was established in the year 1988 as a Sports Hostel                                    
and later it was converted under SAI Operational Scheme namely                                     
SAI Training Centre (STC). This scheme has since be en functioning                                   
from the space provided by the concerned State Government. The STC                                     
centre from Secunderabad was shifted 4 times as per  the convenience                                      
of the State Government. The facilities at STC Secunderabad at Saroor nagar                                
were also provided by the State Government of Telangana. Howev er,                                    
the facilities for Hockey and Athletics were not available at the Centre.                                   

In addition to this, the residential accommodation was also  not sufficient. Sports 
Authority of Telangana offered to provide the facili ties at                                   
Gachibowli Stadium for STC,      where sufficient accommodation    and playing facilities 
for Hockey, Athletics, and Indoor hall are   available in be tter condition. As the 
Indoor stadium at Gachibowli is not sufficient for Gymnastics    training, the training of 
Gymnastics inmates is being held at Saroornagar Centre.   Keeping in view the 
availability of better sports infrastructure and detailed discussion, with the officials of 
State Government  
of Telangana, it was decided to shift STC Secunderab ad to  Gachibowli  stadium, 
where it will benefit maximum sports  disciplines viz., Athlet ics, Hockey, Kabaddi, 
Handball, Judo, etc. 
  On request of some of the Gymnastic trainees who had approached SAI for allowing them 
to stay at the hostel at Gachibowli till their exams  are completed, the same was agreed. 
These gymnasts are residing at STC, Secunderabad, Gachibowli.
 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.3 The Committee felt that the facilities of Wrestling and Boxing are praise worthy, 
which is responsible for this Centre bringing out so many World renowned Sports-
persons. However, this excellence needs to be replicated for other Sports disciplines too. 
The Committee feels that the Athletics Tracks and turf for hockey need to be improved 
and brought at par with the International level incorporating the latest technology and 
sports facilities. The Committee also felt that in view of the forthcoming Rio Olympics in 
2016, the Sports Authorities should focus more on the medal prospective sports 
disciplines like Wrestling, Boxing, Weight-lifting, Athletics etc., where India 
traditionally have been strong, though other disciplines should also be given its fair share 
of attention so as to bring laurels for the Country.                                                                                              
(Para 37) 
 
Action Taken 
 
Athletic Track: There are two athletic tracks at the complex of NRC, Sonepat out of 
which one is synthetic and the other is grassy. The sy nthetic athletic track was laid by 
CPWD in 2010. Since then, the track is being used regularly b y National Campers, SAI 
trainees and players from other institutions.
 
As far as improvement of the facilities is concerne d, constant efforts are being made 
for upgradation of the existing sports facilities. 
Synthetic Hockey Field: The existing synthetic hockey surface was laid by CPW D in 
the year 2008 and taken over by SAI in 2009. Since t hen, the playfield is being used 
regularly by the SAI trainees as well as players from other institutions. After lapse of 
about seven years and regular use, the condition of the turf has deteriorated and it has 
become slippery which may cause injury to the players during practice. Efforts were made 
for watering and cleaning of the same regularly but to no avail. 
In view of above the relaying of Hockey synthetic Tur f is under consideration.
Archery, Athletics, Badminton, Boxing, Hockey, Shooting , Tennis, &Wrestling were 
the key disciplines for the preparation of sportspe rsons for Rio Olympics 2016. The 
National Coaching Camp in these disciplines except T ennis were organized on 
continuous basis wherein sportspersons were provided with all the requisite facilities for 

their preparations, such as wholesome nutritious di et, food supplements, 
equipments, state- of-the-art infrastructure, lodging & travelling facilities, servic es of 
reputed Indian and Foreign Coaches/Supporting staff, Scientific & M edical support, 
Sports Kit etc. besides financial assistance for their abroad tr aining and participation in 
International Competitions in India and abroad. Tennis players being professionals were 
on international circuit as per their specific programmes. 
In addition to the above, Government also provided financial assistance to i ndividual 
sportspersons from the scheme 'Target Olympic Podium' (T OP). Under this scheme 
individualized needs of identified sportspersons fo r the 2016 Rio Olympic Games 
were catered to. There was no shortage of funds und er this scheme; identified 
sportspersons were fully financially assisted for th eir advance training under world 
renowned coaches /experts at reputed training centr es worldwide. Identified 
sportspersons are also being provided with personal equipment and training gears of their 
choice. 
In the 2012 London Olympic Games, a total of 81 sportspersons including Men Hockey 
team had qualified and participated. 119 sportspersons inc luding 16 members each of 
Hockey teams men and women qualified for participat ion in Rio Olympics. This was 
India’s largest ever contingent for Olympic Games. 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.4 The Committee recommends that SAI should provide more funds to NIS, Patiala 
for the purchase of equipments so that there are no short-comings in the efforts being put 
in by these athletes for the upcoming Olympics Games, 2016. The Committee also 
recommends that an Indoor Stadium for Athletics should be built for the year and practice 
for athletes. The Committee also directed NIS, Patiala to have interface with State Bank 
of Patiala (SBP) and other PSUs in Punjab for sponsorship and adoption of certain events 
and players who have been shortlisted for International event. The State Bank of Patiala 
(SBP) had promised to help the centre. The Institutes may identify the areas where these 
PSUs are able to provide financial assistance. The Committee was also apprised that to 
participate in certain international events, players needed coaching in foreign centres. 
However, due to shortage of funds this was not possible. The Committee feels that the 
medal winning prospects should be given coaching in foreign centres and shortage of 
funds should not come in the way. The Committee was also apprised that in Fencing 
there are many medal winning prospects.              
                                                                                                                       (Para 51) 
 
 
Action Taken 
As per requirement of the National Campers in Athle tics &Coaches concerned supply 
order for the procurement of imported Javelin was placed. 
Estimate for the construction of Indoor Synthetic Athletics Track has been obtain ed 
from NPCC Ltd. It is being modified as per requirement of the coac hes concerned. On 
finalizing the same, it shall be submitted for approval of the competent authority. 
Matter regarding seeking sponsorship from PSUs like Banking sector for the training 
equipments, foreign exposure to elite sportspersons  & Infrastructure development 

has been taken up with the General Manager, SBP vid e letter dated 20.11.2015 and 
10.02.2016 respectively. 
The Government also provided financial assistance to individual sportspersons from 
the Scheme Target Olympic Podium (TOP). Under this scheme individualized  needs 
of identified sportspersons for the 2016 Rio Olympic  Games were 
catered to. There 
was no shortage of funds under this scheme; identif ied sportspersons were fully 
financially assisted for their advance training under wor ld renowned coaches /experts at 
reputed training centres worldwide. Identified sportspersons were also prov ided with 
personal equipment and training gears of their choice. 
 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.5 The Committee is seized of the fact that many of the outstanding sportspersons of 
Yesteryears are living in penurious circumstances. The Committee desires that the 
Department of Sports should prepare a database of such players so that initiative may be 
taken by the Department of Sports to alleviate the financial condition of such 
sportsperson of yesteryears who have won medal or participated in National/International 
events/Championships  by providing lump sum financial assistance/lifelong pension 
facility, etc. The Committee expects to send a progress report in this regard within a 
month.  
                                                                                                                       (Para 117) 
 
Recommendation/Observations  
2.6 In a Country of such a humongous sports potential, the Committee hopes that this 
record can only get better. The Committee notes that we have to realize that where we 
stand for Rio 2016. The performance of Indian contingent in the previous participation in 
Olympics is mostly about failure. It is merely a question of when and where our 
sportsperson failed and blame game, as usual, where accusations are exchanged among 
the involved people who refuse to accept any responsibility. The defeat and losses bring 
disappointment. The first and foremost question to be asked is whether team or 
sportsperson fell short of expectations on account of poor training, exposure and lack of 
amenities. The Department of Sports/SAI, National Sports Federations etc., are in the 
Process of zeroing in on the sportspersons possessing the medal winning prospects. 
Keeping in view the breakdown of Indian contingent in past Olympics, the Committee 
expects the Sportspersons to stand up to the pressure of Olympics and not to give a below 
par performance.                                       
                                                                                                                     (Para 119) 
 
Action Taken 
The Ministry had launched a scheme called ‘Target Olympic Podium Scheme’ for medal 
prospects identified for 2016 Rio Olympic. Government provided financial assistance to 
individual sportspersons from the Scheme ‘Target Olympic Podium (TOP) ’. Under this 
scheme individualized needs of identified sportsper sons for the 2016 Rio Olympic 
Games were 
catered to. Identified sportspersons were fully financially assisted for their 
advance training under world renowned coaches/experts at r eputed training centres 
worldwide. Under the Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NS Fs), all 

the requisite requirement including acclimatization of Indian sportspersons were 
planned for Rio-Olympics, 2016 as a part of ACTC plan of different sports disc iplines. 
Identified sportspersons were also provided with personal equipment and training gears of 
their choice.
 
In the last 2012 London Olympic Games, a total of 81 sportspersons including Men 
Hockey team had qualified and participated. 119 sportspers ons including 16 members 
each of Hockey  
teams (men and women) qualified for participation i n Rio Olympics. This was India ’s 
largest ever contingent for Olympic Games. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER-III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES 
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
COMMITTEE 
Recommendation/Observations  
3.1 From the deliberations of the Committee with CPSUs, it has come to notice that 
CPSUs are not adequately familiar with the existence of the National Sports 
Development Fund (NSDF) and they are by and large linking the NSDF with CSR 
activities. The Committee, therefore, directs the Department of Sports as well as the 
Sports Authority of India to take all possible measures immediately to educate all the 
CPSUs on the difference between NSDF and their role in CSR so that funds can be 
mobilized for NSDF without any further delay. The Committee notes that the way the 
CPSUs are participating on development and promotion of sports can be made more 
rationalized and contributing to the broad-basing of National Sports. The Committee also 
notes with anguish that this issue was also pointed out in its previous Report on the same 
subject, however, no action seems to have been taken in this regard and in case the 
awareness and familiarity about the NSDF among the CPSUs continue to languish as on 
date, the very purpose of the NSDF would be defeated and the Department of Sports 
/Sports Authority of India would be responsible for the failure on their parts to popularize 
the same.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                          (Para 18) 
 
Recommendation/Observations  
3.2 The Committee, after its deliberations with PSBs, feels that though there are 
Sports Control Boards in these Banks, yet they are not aware of the requirement for 
contribution to the National Sports Development Fund for promotion of excellence in 
sports, as well as board-basing of sports. The Committee notes that the Department of 
Sports and the Sports Authority of India have not properly familiarized NSDF to them 
and the role required from them in this regard. The Committee appreciates the periodic 
encouragement given by Banks to sports as well as sportspersons in the form of holding 
tournaments/sports events, cash awards, contribution as sponsorships, etc. However, co-
ordination with Department of Sports/SAI is lacking. The Committee recommends that 
Department of Sports/SAI should make concerted efforts in co-coordinating with them in 
promotion of sports in the perspective of extant National Sports Policy and encouraging 
them to make contribution to the National Sports Development Fund.  
                                                                                                                        (Para 25) 
 
Action Taken 
The Government is regularly interacting with CPSUs/PSBs for contribution to the NSDF. 
They are also encouraged to contribute to the NSDF under CSR (Corporate Social 
Responsibility). Further, the Ministry has decided to organize meetings with important 
PSUs in Delhi in association with the Department of Public Enterprises and also with 
PSBs in association with the Department of Financial Services for creating awareness 
about NSDF and their role in CSR in order to mobilize funds for NSDF. The Ministry has 
also written letters to CMDs of PSUs in Coal Sector, Petroleum Sector and Banks for 
contributing funds to NSDF. 

The Ministry will compile a list of potential donors both in the private sector and public 
sector. The Ministry will write to such potential donors requiring them to contribute to 
NSDF. The Ministry will also organize seminars/workshops in major cities to create 
awareness about NSDF. The Department will also depute its teams to potential donors 
explaining them about existence of NSDF and requesting them to contribute to NSDF. 
The Ministry will also prepare publicity material such as brochures, pamphlets, videos 
etc. about NSDF and distribute the same among donors.  As regards promotion of sports 
and recruitment of sportspersons, the matter has already been taken up by this 
Department with the DOPT and a committee has also been formed to look into this and 
other issues. The Committee ’s specific recommendations on mandatory 5% quota fo r 
employment of sportspersons in Govt. vacancies have been forwarded to DOPT for 
necessary action. 
 
Observation of the Committee: 
The Committee  notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the outcom e of the 
steps initiated by the Department/SAI in educating the Central Public Sector 
Undertakings and Public Sector Banks about the National Sports Development 
Fund and the Corporate Social Responsibility.  The Committee would also like to 
know whether this has resulted in enhancing the contribution to NSDF by the 
CPSUs/PSBs,  The Committee accordingly, directs the Department of Sports is 
provide the Committee details of contributions, to NSDF made in the last three 
years, year wise and company wise.  The Committee further directs the Departme nt 
of Sports to apprise the Committee of the status as to number of potential donors in 
private sector were approached and contributions  received from them.  The  
Committee, however, would like to know the end result from the Departmen t/SAI 
about its specific recommendation of mandatory 5 per cent quota for employment of 
sportspersons in Government vacancies.  The Committee would appreciate if the 
Department/SAI pursues the matter with DOPT vigorously. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observations  
3.3 The Committee notes that the State Governments gets fund assistance for 
promotion of sports from the Central Government through the Department of Sports and 
the need and identification of projects are made under different extant schemes. The 
Committee recommends that it would be an appreciative move if the Department of 
Sports and the SAI interact with the State Governments for encouraging the recruitment 
of sportspersons in vacancies arising out in the domain of State Governments of Andhra 
Pradesh and Telangana covering their autonomous units as well. The Committee directs 
to provide a status note in this regard from the Department of Sports within a month.                                        
                                                                                                                         (Para 28) 
 
Action Taken 
Department of Sports has written letters to the State Government of Andhra Pradesh and 
State Government of Telangana to make provisions for recruitment of sportspersons in 
vacancies arising out in their domain and also to make recruitment of meritorious 
sportspersons against vacancies reserved for them in relaxation of the recruitment 

procedure, to the extent these including all other reservations under existing orders do not 
exceed 50% of the total number of vacancies proposed to be filled by direct recruitment. 
If a request is received from the State Government of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, an 
Officer from the Department of Sports can be deputed to Andhra Pradesh and Telangana 
to discuss the issue of recruitment of sportspersons by the State Governments 
Observation of the Committee 
The Committee notes with concern that Department of Sports did not furnish the 
status note as desired by it.  The Committee reiterates its observation and directs 
the Department of Sports to submit the same at the earliest.  Recruitment of 
meritorious  sportspersons against the vacancies reserved for them especially in the 
domain of State Governments has been an area of concern for the Committee f or 
quite sometime.  The Committee feels that the Department/SAI should have a pro-
active approach in the matter.  Department/SAI should coordinate with the State 
Governments to fill in the vacancies reserved for meritorious sportspersons at the 
earliest.  The Committee reiterates that the Department/SAI should also create a 
database covering all the States/UTs having details of number of  posts reserved f or 
meritorious sportspersons, filled up and vacant vacancies alongwith the sports 
disciplines covered. 
 
Recommendation/Observations  
3.4 The Committee appreciates the efforts undertaken by the PSUs and PSBs to 
promote sports. Some of the PSUs like SAIL, BHEL etc. and Banks have invested a lot in 
the development of sports in the Country. However, the Committee observes that most of 
the PSUs and PSBs have no definite sports policy for promotion of sports in the Country 
and recruitment of sportspersons. It was brought to the notice of the Committee that most 
of the PSUs are following the directives of Central Government which are issued from 
time to time. The Committee is unhappy to note that most of the PSUs are not aware of 
National ports Development (NSDF). Also no funds from CSR are allocated for 
promotion of sports. Therefore, the Committee recommends that Sports Authority of 
India (SAI) should undertake efforts to make all PSUs and Banks aware of this fund so 
that more contribution can be put forward for the promotion and development of sports in 
the Country. The Committee also observes that SAI needs to tie up with the concerned 
agencies so that a definite sports policy can be adopted by the PSUs and Banks for 
promotion of sports in the perspective of the National Sports Policy, 2001, which 
envisage promotion of excellence in Sports and also broad-basing of Sports. Further, a 
policy needs to be formulated so that certain percentage of the funds earmarked for CSR 
activities can be allotted for the promotion and development of sports in the Country. The 
recruitment of Sportspersons in PSUs/PSBs is being done as per the Guidelines of DoPT, 
which stipulates reservation upto 5% in existing vacancies. This implies that there is no 
minimum Cap for employment of Sportsperson in the said Guidelines. The Committee, 
therefore, strongly recommends that DoPT should make necessary amendments in the 
Guidelines for recruitments of Sportspersons so that the mandatory 5% quota of 
Sportspersons of arising vacancies is filled up. 
                                                                                                                         (Para 86) 
 
Action Taken 

As already stated above in reply to recommendation nos. 5,18 and 25, the Government is 
regularly in touch with CPSUs/PSBs for contribution to NSDF under CSR. Further, the 
Ministry has decided to organize meetings with important PSUs in Delhi in association 
with the Department of Public Enterprises and also with Publics Sector Banks in 
association with Department of Financial Services for creating awareness about NSDF 
and their role in CSR in order to mobilize funds for NSDF. The Ministry has also written 
letters to CMDs of PSUs in Coal Sector, Petroleum Sector and Banks for contributing 
funds to NSDF.  
The Ministry will compile a list of potential donors both in the private sector and public 
sector. The Ministry will write to such potential donors requiring them to contribute to 
NSDF. The Ministry will also organize seminars/workshops in major cities to create 
awareness about NSDF. The Department will also depute its teams to potential donors 
explaining them about existence of NSDF and requesting them to contribute to NSDF. 
The Ministry will also prepare publicity material such as brochures, pamphlets, videos 
etc. about NSDF and distribute the same among donors. 
The matter of recruitment of sportspersons has already been taken up by this Department 
with the DOPT and a committee has also been formed to look into this and other issues. 
The Committee’s specific recommendations on mandatory 5% quota for employment of 
sportspersons in Govt. vacancies have been forwarded to DOPT for necessary action. 
 
Observation of the Committee 
The Committee while appreciating the efforts put in by the Department/SAI in 
educating CPSUs/PSBs on promotion of sports and contribution to NSDF, would  
like to reiterate that its specific  recommendation has been to encourage all 
CPSUs/PSBs to have definite sports policy for promotion and development of 
sports.  The Committee accordingly observes that the Department/SAI should take 
concrete steps in this direction by involving Government organizations, nurturing 
talents, and designing specialized programmes for overall development of sports.  
The Committee is of the concerted opinion that organizing 
meetings/workshops/seminars with CPSUs/PSBs alone  would not make any change 
at the ground level.  If the Department/SAI earnestly desires to create a sports 
culture, it should take a pro-active role in promoting sports by encouraging 
CPSUs/PSBs to, not only invest in sports on a large scale, but also to provide career 
incentives to the sportspersons then only the sports activity will get a required boost.  
Recommendation/Observations  
3.5 The Committee observes that the State of Haryana has not yet submitted the 
utilization certificates amounting to Rs. 3,34,84,178/-. The Committee, therefore, feels 
that the Department of Sports should take up this issue with the State Government of 
Haryana. The Department should insist on the submission of UCs by the State 
Government of Haryana on different policies and schemes in promotion of sports and 
sportspersons on an urgent basis and the Committee expects a status Note in this regard 
within a month. 
(Para 
102) 
 
Action Taken 

The matter has been taken up with the Additional Chief Secretary, Sports & Youth 
Affairs Department, Government of Haryana for expediting the submission of Unutilized 
Certificates(UCs) or refund of the grant along with interest as per provisions of GFRs, 
2005. 
Observation of the Committee  
The Committee is not satisfied by merely taking up the matter with Additional 
Chief Secretary.  The Committee believes that in past also, the Department might  
have taken it up with the State Government.  This is just not enough.  The non-
submissions of UCs by State Governments is not an exception, but this happens in 
large no. of cases.  The Committee impress es upon the Department of Sports  to 
address this problem at level of Minister and ensure  that UCs are received in time 
so that the schemes do not suffer.   The Committee desires that a detailed  note on  
further action taken  by the Department be submitted to the Committee.  
Recommendation/Observations  
3.6 The Committee on the basis of deliberations with PSUs/PSBs for promotion of 
Sports reiterates its views that Public and Private Sector Undertakings as well as Banks / 
Financial Institutions etc., may be encouraged by the Department of Sports/SAI to adopt 
one Sports Discipline or can take total responsibility of scouting talents and its nurturing 
including their participation in various National and International Events. On the 
reciprocal basis, the concerned donor should have its Nominee in the concerned National 
Federal/Association. The Committee is seized of the fact that, GAIL has orally 
committed that they would adopt one Centre of SAI. The ONGC has proposed to support 
Wrestling players. Further M/s Damodar Valley Corporation has also offered to support 
two athletes under Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme for which requisite 
information as requested by them has been furnished to them. The Committee directs that 
the Department of Sports and SAI should nominate an exclusive Nodal Officer in each 
region for co-coordinating with PSUs/PSBs so that they can contribute to the NSDF as 
well as adopt a Sports Discipline/Game or a Centre. The Committee directs the 
Department of Sports/SAI to submit a monthly progress report to the Committee to this 
effect.                                                                               (Para 116) 
 
Action Taken 
It has been decided that Regional Heads of SAI will be nominated as Nodal Officers for 
coordinating with PSUs/PSBs. The Department has decided to organize meetings in 
Delhi with CMDs of PSUs and PSBs for creating awareness about NSDF. The 
Department has already written letters to CMDs of PSUs in Coal Sector, Petroleum 
Sector and Banks for contributing funds to NSDF. 
 
Observation of the Committee 
The Committee desires to know the impact on the PSUs, PSBs with regard to 
contribution towards  NSDF since the regional nodal officers were appointed.  The 
Committee may also be apprised of the efforts made by t hese nodal officers in that 
regard. 
Recommendation/Observations  
3.7 The Committee on the basis of its deliberations with sportsperson and various 
stake holders in the field of sports decided to assess the rate of employability of 

sportspersons in the country. The Committee, therefore, desires that the Department of 
Sports should prepare basic database on the current status of employment in Central 
Government/State Government departments, their PSUs, and PSBs of sportspersons 
representing and winning medals in national/international events/championships. A status 
note is required to be sent to the Committee within a month.                                                                            
(Para 118) 
 
Action Taken 
Regarding preparation of database of sportspersons and current status of employment in 
Central Government/State Government Departments, their PSUs and PSBs of 
sportspersons representing and winning medals in various national/international 
championships, the Ministry has written letters to all State Governments, 
Ministries/Departments to furnish details of sportspersons employed in Central 
Government and State Government Offices. 
Observation of the Committee 
The Committee may be apprised of said details and direct the Department of 
Sports  to pursue with all concerned so as to obtain the requisite details.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED 
BY 
GOVERNMENT 
 
I. VISIT TO THIRUVANANTHAPURAM, MUMBAI AND UDAIPUR 
MUMBAI  
  
(B) MUMBAI 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
1.0  During interaction with the Committee, it was informed that the Bank is 
willing to support/sponsor talented/promising sportspersons. However, no proposal was 
received by them from SAI. In response, SAI Officials informed that the Ministry of 
Youth Affairs & Sports has already written to Department of Financial Services. The 
Committee, therefore, directed SAI to give specific proposal to the Bank and not just a 
general routine communication, which would lose its importance.  (Para 46) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.1  The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports has sent specific proposals to 
the organizations which attended meeting of Standing Committee on HRD at 
Thiruvananthapuram, Mumbai & Udaipur from 13 th to 20 th February, 2016, at Delhi on 
14.6.16 and at Chennai, Vishakhapatnam, Bhopal, Ujjain and Indore from 27 th June to 5th 
July, 2016 to support sports.  
1.2  Further, the Government has been regularly interacting with corporate 
entities both in public sector and private sector for adopting one specific discipline for 
taking the overall responsibility including talent scouting, training and competitive 
exposure of the sports persons. It has been decided that the Regional Heads of SAI will 
be coordinating with PSUs/Banks. A CSR Brochure on SAI activities giving details of 
various SAI Centres under various SAI Sports Promotional Schemes, 10 Regional & 02 
Academic Institutions has been prepared giving various options for potential CSR 
partners to come up with proposals as per their convenience and availability of funds.  

1.3  A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Hon`ble Minister of State  
(Independent Charge)   on 24 th November, 2016 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with 46 
Central Public Sector Undertakings and Public Sector Banks on issues related to 
promotion of sports and contribution to NSDF.   There was good response and it emerged 
that there should be synergy of efforts being made by various organizations for 
development of sports. Department of sports will work towards bringing in the said 
synergy.  
 
(C) UDAIPUR 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
1.4  The Committee lauded the effort of IIFCL, Bank of Baroda and Oriental 
Bank of Commerce for their contribution extended for promotion of sports and these 
Organizations will set a very big example for the benefit of the Sports in the Country as a 
whole. The Committee urges the other organizations to start looking into this aspect and 
go for contributing to this noble cause, which will ultimately contribute to making India a 
strong and confident Sporting Nation. The Committee also endorses the idea of 
sponsoring of deserving Sportspersons by Banks and PSUs or the adoption of a Sporting 
Centre, preferably in a rural or backward region of the Country, from where the 
unpolished raw talents would definitely arise.                                            (Para 104) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.5  A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Hon`ble Minister of State  
(Independent Charge) on 24 th November, 2016 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with 46 
Central Public Sector Undertakings and Public Sector Banks on issues related to 
promotion of sports and contribution to NSDF.  There was good response and it emerged 
that there should be synergy of efforts being made by various organizations for 
development of sports. Department of sports will work towards bringing in the said 
synergy.  
1.6  Sports Authority of India (SAI) also approaches CPSUs and other entities 
from time to time for financial support in implementing its schemes. In a new initiative 

SAI has identified over 36 centres to attract CSR funding.  Ministry of Youth Affairs and 
Sports has already taken up the issue with the PSUs and PSBs urging them to contribute

II. LOCAL VISIT TO JAWAHAR LAL NEHRU STADIUM 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
  
1.7  The Committee appreciates the effort put in by Indian Railways for 
promotion of sports in India and the initiatives taken by it at various levels starting from 
Zonal level to National and International levels. The Committee suggests that since 
Indian Railways has a vast Network across the Country, it should consider setting up of 
Sports Centres in rural areas also, which will also improve their outreach as well as 
increase their pool of Sportspersons. The Committee also recommends that SAI should 
co-ordinate with Indian Railways in setting up these rural centres and also provide 
expertise.          (Para 128) 
 
Action Taken

being run by the Ministry of Railways  are (1) Hockey Academy at Kapurthala, (2) 
Throw Academy at Jaipur and (3) Wrestling Academy in Kishanganj, Delhi. Young 
sportspersons of adjoining areas including rural areas practice at these academies. 
Recommendations of the Hon ’ble Committee regarding setting up such more centres in 
rural areas and taking SAI expertise shall be considered while setting up such more 
academies in future. 
1.9  Sports Authority of India have informed that they will provide available 
expertise as per need / requirement of Railways. However, most of the SAI Centers under 
its various Sports Promotional Schemes are in rural / semi-urban areas. The number of

will be provided and sincere efforts will be made to attract CSR partners to complete the 
ongoing / new projects. SAI is making all out efforts to consolidate and bring the existing 
centres up to the mark.  
 
Recommendations/Observation 
 
1.10  The Committee notes that there is still some confusion among the PSUs 
regarding NSDF and CSR. The Committee observes that CSR comes under the 
Companies Act, while NSDF comes under Society Endowment Act. Hence, contribution 
under CSR cannot be equated to NSDF. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
Department of Sports, in coordination with Department of Public Enterprises and 
Department of Corporate Affairs, should immediately undertake with right earnest, to 
educate the PSUs/PSBs about the functioning of NSDF as well as the process of making 
contributions thereto.        (Para 140)

(Independent Charge) on 24 th November, 2016 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with 46 
Central Public Sector Undertakings and Public Sector Banks on issues related to 
promotion of sports and contribution to NSDF.   A booklet on NSDF was also distributed 
among PSUs and PSBs. There was good response and it emerged that there should be 
synergy of efforts being made by various organizations for development of sports.

I. VISIT OF THE COMMITTEE TO THIRUVANANTHAPURAM, 
MUMBAI AND UDAIPUR  
(C) UDAIPUR 
Recommendations/observations 
 
3.0  The Committee directs that an updated accounts of the expenditure made 
from this fund should be provided to the Committee along with the performance and 
achievement of the beneficiaries to whom this expenditure was incurred. The Committee 
also strongly suggests that the Department of Sports should keep a record of the 
contributions made to the NSDF and also pursue with other PSBs/PSUs on keeping a 
database of their contributions.        (Para 75) 
 
Action Taken 
 
3.1  Details of contributions to NSDF is attached as Annexure I . Details of 
assistance provided from NSDF is attached as Annexure II . A copy of Balance sheet and 
Income and expenditure account for the period ending 31.3.16 of NSDF are enclosed as 
Annexure III. (The said accounts have been internally audited by Charte red accountant of 
NSDF and CAG has been requested for conducting its audit.) A statement giving details 
of NSDF assistance provided to sportspersons and organisations till date is summarised 
as under:- 
Direct assistance to sportspersons for training and purchase of equipment 
(This includes assistance released direct to the athletes under Target 
Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme, which is intended specifically for 
preparation of Olympics 2016 & 2020) 
 
Rs. 46.52 crore 
Assistance to institutes / organisations for development of sports 
infrastructure, training camp, sports events etc. 
 
Rs. 52.28 crore 
Cash Award and other incentives / welfare 
 
Rs. 4.49 crore 
Total Rs. 103.29 crore 
 

3.2  In addition, the NSDF had released Rs. 20.00 crore to the Sports Authority 
of India (SAI) under Target Olympic (TOP) Scheme for further release to the athletes for 
their training, purchase of equipment etc.  Annexure IV gives major 
performance/achievements of NSDF beneficiaries.  
Comments of Committee 
 
3.3  The Committee appreciates the assistance rendered to the 
Sportspersons of the Country through the NSDF.  The Committee notes that these 
assistance varied from Rs. 14, 101/- (for Ms. Arpita M, Athletics and Ms. Sarjubala 
Devi, Boxer) to Rs. 635,02,982/- (Shri Manavjit Singh Sandhu, Shooter) and Rs. 
615,86,657/- (Shri Abhinav Bindra, Shooter). The Committee also notes that a major 
chunk of the fund has been spent on the shooting team while an Olympics Discipli ne 
like Gymnastics got Rs. 63,48, 787/- for the whole team.  The Committee does not 
wish to question the wisdom of the Department for such an allocation of funds. 
However, the Committee feels that type of Sports Discipline should not be the only 
criteria for fixing the quantum of assistance provided to a Sportsperson.  There 
should be some criteria  to link the  quantum of  assistance to the performance of  
the Sportsperson. The Committee wishes that any discipline where having medal 
winning prospects should also be given same level of assistance.   
3.4  The Committee further noticed that the names of young and budding 
Sportspersons are missing from the list of beneficiaries and most of the names in the 
achievers list seem to be the seniors/retiring/retired Sportspersons.  The Committee, 
therefore, feels that more names of budding Sportspersons should appear on the list 
of beneficiaries enabling them to excel in their performances. 
3.5   The Committee further notes that a total amount of Rs. 98,75,34,945/- has 
been received as donations under NSDF, while the matching contribution by the 
Government of India is Rs. 76,45,01,675/- only.  The Committee notes with concern 
that Department of Sports has failed to provide the matching grant in NSDF vis-a-
vis the contribution received to fund.  As is evident the Department of Sports is yet 
in contribute more than Rs 22 crores in to order is match the contribution.  The 

Committee impresses upon the Department to provide the matching grant at the 
earliest so that the very objective of NSDF is fulfilled. 
 
III. VISIT OF THE COMMITTEE TO CHENNAI, VISHAKHAPATNAM, 
BHOPAL, UJJAIN AND INDORE 
 
Recommendations/Observation 
 
3.6 The Committee further notes that many of the Banks are willing to sponsor the 
talented young sportspersons but there is a hiatus in the communication between SAI and 
the Banks. The Committee, therefore, recommends that SAI needs to give specific 
proposals to the concerned Banks and not a general routine communication in this regard, 
as the importance of the objective gets vitiated. The Committee also recommends the SAI 
to have a regular platform with the representatives PSUs/PSBs as well as Department of 
P.E. and DFS to give effect to this fund so that Indian Sports /Sportspersons do not suffer 
due to the lack of funds/support and by 2020 Olympics, we will be in a better position to 
be among the top ten Sporting Nations in the world.                               (Para 227) 
Action Taken 
3.7  The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports has sent specific proposals to 
the organizations which attended meeting of Standing Committee on HRD at 
Thiruvananthapuram, Mumbai and Udaipur from 13 th to 20th February, 2016, at Delhi on 
14th June, 2016; and at Chennai, Vishakhapatnam, Bhopal, Ujjain and Indore from 27 th 
June to 5th July, 2016 to support sports.  
3.8  Further, the Government has been regularly interacting with corporate 
entities both in public sector and private sector for adopting one specific discipline for 
taking the overall responsibility including talent scouting, training and competitive 
exposure of the sports persons. It has been decided that the Regional Heads of SAI will 
be coordinating with PSUs/Banks. A CSR Brochure on SAI activities giving details of 
various SAI Centres under various SAI Sports Promotional Schemes, 10 Regional and 2 
Academic Institutions has been prepared giving various options for potential CSR 
partners to come up with proposals as per their convenience and availability of funds.  

3.9  A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Hon`ble Minister of State 
(Independent Charge) on 24 th November, 2016 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with 46 
Central Public Sector Undertakings and Public Sector Banks on issues related to 
promotion of sports and contribution to NSDF.   There was good response and it emerged 
that there should be synergy of efforts being made by various organizations for 
development of sports. Department of sports will work towards bringing in the said 
synergy. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
3.10  The Committee finds that the reply of the Department gives a vague 
reference to the specific proposals which, according to the recommendation of the 
Committee, should have been given to the organizations/PSUs/PSBs, which were 
present in the Committee’s meeting in Thiruvananthapuram, Mumbai and Udaipur 
from 13 th to 20 th February, 2016, at Delhi on 14 th June, 2016; and at Chennai, 
Vishakhapatnam, Bhopal, Ujjain and Indore from 27 th June to 5 th July, 2016. The 
Department should have given the details of the proposals along with the dates on 
which such proposals were sent and what has been the response of those 
organizations. The Committee, accordingly, desires that all these details be made 
available to the Committee for its consideration.  
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
3.11  The Committee recommends that SAI should take pro-active steps to 
improve infrastructures/coaching facilities in the rural areas, where there is no dearth of 
talents. The Committee, therefore, recommends that SAI should involve Banks in talent 
hunt at the grassroot level like at District Level throughout the Country.   
      (Para 230) 
 
Action Taken 
 
3.12   The Government of India has started Khelo India Scheme in which talent 
identification is major component. SAI will be involved in the programme and it will 
give all stake holders an opportunity to identify a sports talent for grooming for 

excellence. SAI is also launching an online talent hunt portal which is likely to be 
operational by February 2017, which will give opportunity to all gifted and talented 
athletes to apply to SAI for inclusion under various Sports Promotional Schemes. 
Modalities will be worked out once specific proposal are received from banks to identify 
young talents form the rural/tribal area. However, Sports Authority of India is already 
implementing Special Area Games/Sports Training Centre Scheme which caters the need 
of rural/tribal and coastal area in the Country. 
3.13  With respect to improvement of coaching system SAI has entered into a MOU 
with International Council for Coaching Excellence (ICCE) to improve standards of 
coaching & coach improvement. Efforts are already under way to integrate international 
federation recognized certificate courses with our ongoing Diploma Courses. In some 
sports disciplines e.g. Football, we have already implemented this scheme. Other 
disciplines will also be gradually covered. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
3.14 The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department/SAI to 
improve the infrastructures/coaching facilities in rural areas as well as the creation 
of online talent hunt portal likely to be launched soon.  These steps would de finitely 
help the rural talents to have easy access to the facilities and take part in 
competitions easily.  The Committee further recommends that the Department/SAI 
should now take steps to give wider publicity of all these schemes/competition/talent 
hunt programmes not only through online applications but also through posters, 
radio announcements, TV ads etc., in local languages/dialects, which are more 
connected to the rural youths. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.15 The Committee finds that the majority of the appointment has been done in the 
non-officer category. The Committee recommends that player who has played at the 
National level should be inducted at the Officer Cadre (Group A). The Committee further 
recommends that sportspersons who played at the State and District level should be 
recruited in Group B or C.  (Para 233) 

 
Action Taken 
 
3.16  As per existing guidelines on the subject of recruitment and promotion of 
meritorious sportspersons, the existing policy provide recruitment at Group “C” level 
only.  The policy is under review. A committee comprising representatives of Department 
of Sports and Sports Authority of India has deliberated on the issue.  The recruitment of 
Olympic/Para Olympic  medal winners to higher level posts is one among the issues 
which is being examined.   
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
3.17  The Committee wishes that the Department/SAI should pursue the matter 
with the Committee constituted by the Department of Sports/SAI to deliberate on 
the matter and the views of the Committee on HRD should also be communicated to 
them.  This Committee feels that in order to attract talents in sports, it is imperative 
that the Government should provide a source of livelihood to the Sportspersons as 
their active lifespan in very limited unlike other professions.  Contrarily, youngsters 
would not opt for Sports as a career, if there is no secured future for them to fall 
back on, after their active Sports career is over.

REPORT
The Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development deals with the action taken by the Government on the recommendations/observations contained
in its Two Hundred eighty-third Report on the subject “The Implementation of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and
Mid-Day-Meal Scheme” pertaining to the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Department of School
Education and Literacy. The 283rd Report was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 20th June,
2017. The Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of School Education and Literacy) vide
its communication dated 29th June, 2017 furnished its Action Taken replies to the Committee.
2. Action Taken Notes received from the Government in respect of the recommendations contained in
the 283rd Report have been categorized as follows:

40, 40.1, 42,43, 44 and 45 Total – 19

Paras –  Nil Total - Nil

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY GOVERNMENT
Recommendations/Observations
34.1 The Committee, therefore, recommends to initiate the pilot project of establishing the Smart Classes in
Government schools, in fact, through which teaching–learning process would be effective using computer
enabled techniques, wherein teaching by the use of multi-media projector is executed and Smart Boards are
used, which have more visualization of lessons for students. A comprehensive viable target should be set for
successful functioning of Smart-Classes in Govt. schools and a status note be provided to the Committee.
Action Taken
Under the Innovation Head, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) provides support for Computer aided Learning
(CAL) facilities upto ` 50 lakhs per district per year. The focus of CAL is to maximize coverage in Upper
Primary Schools with special emphasis on Science and Mathematics. During 2016-17, an amount of
` 31195.06 lakh has been allocated for CAL in 8226 government upper primary schools including ` 16493.63
lakh for Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (RAA).
Recommendations/Observations
41. The Committee further recommends that for intensification of MDMS, it should be incumbent on the
nodal Ministry to review the infrastructure development meant for MDMS in the meetings of Steering-cum-
Monitoring Committee (SMC) and representatives of other nodal Ministries which run the infrastructure
development schemes of MDMS should be invited to these meetings.
Action Taken
The mid day meal scheme covered 10.03 Crore children studying in 11.50 lakh Government and
Government aided schools, Special Training Centres and Madrasas & Maqtabs supported under SSA on
daily basis during 2015-16.  In order to monitor the scheme of such magnitude and vastness,  the MDM
guidelines provide for setting up of Steering-cum-Monitoring Committees at National, State and District
Levels. The State Level Steering-cum-Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) headed by Chief Secretary of the
State advises the State on the implementation of the Scheme and discusses issues requiring convergence
with other Departments in the State.  It has been made mandatory that the Annual Work Plan & Budget of
the State should be approved by SLSMC. During 2015-16 37 meetings of the SLSMC were held in various
States/UTs. During 2016-17, 8 meetings of SLSMC have been held.  The representative of the MHRD is
also invited in the SLSMC meetings.
2

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
Recommendations/Observations
28. On the basis of deliberations with various stakeholders in the field of elementary education at places
of visit described in proceeding paragraphs, the Committee notes that Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) was
launched in 2000-01. However , the precursor of this programme was District Primary Education Programme
(DPEP), launched way back in 1993-94 with an aim of achieving the objective of universal primary
education. There is no denying the fact that for both DPEP and SSA, the major thrust is to ensure universal
enrolment in elementary schools and remove social and gender gaps in schooling. Back in reckoning, the 2%
education cess was set rolling in 2004 and, in fact, there was no opposition whatsoever for imposition of this
levy. The Committee appreciates the endeavor made by the Government towards the universal enrolment
goal for schools in India, which has led to the fact that almost all children are enrolled in school today. The
Committee, on the other hand, is intrigued to note that while the enrolment picture continues to improve; on
the learning front, the story is far from satisfactory. In Arithmetic, only a little over half of all children
involved in Standard V could do a 2 digit subtraction problem with borrowing.
Action Taken
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has made significant progress in achieving near universal access and
equity. However, imparting quality education to children at elementary level is the major challenge and
therefore, reorienting the SSA programme towards quality is the main emphasis of the Department. Central
Government, along with State and UT Governments has taken various initiatives for improving the quality of
education, the details of which are attached at Annexure-I.
Recommendations/Observations
28.1 The Committee, therefore, emphatically recommends that Central Government should undertake all
initiatives for the States and focus on ensuring that children are learning well and the States should also
resort to their own measures in a time bound sustainable manner to understand what is the level of students
in terms of learning, and the means to determine improvement in basic learning. The Committee also
recommends that the need of the hour is to shift the policy and practice from input-based expenditure to
outcome-focused achievement for implementation of SSA.
29. The Committee further notes that one of the prime challenges is to get much more effective utilization
of the resources that are spent on elementary education which is the backbone of SSA. Effective spending
implies that the expenditure is incurred on progress towards goals, especially in terms of improving learning
outcomes of children in elementary schools.
Action Taken (28.1 & 29)
For the financial year 2016-17, the Project Approval Board (PAB) of the SSA decided that 10% of the
total outlay shall be utilized for quality related initiatives alone under the SSA as against approximately 6% in
previous years. Accordingly, activities related to quality interventions through SSA were approved in the
Annual Plans for all States and UTs.
3

4
To enable this, the Department categorized all interventions under the SSA in three categories where
Category II is related to interventions for improvement in quality and learning outcomes. These include
Teacher Training, Academic Support through BRC/CRC, Learning Enhancement Programme (LEP),
Innovation fund for CAL, Library, Teacher Grant, TLE for New Schools, Transport/Escort facility, Special
Training for Age appropriate admission of OoSC, Innovation, Community Mobilization and SMC Training.
While releasing the funds under SSA, all States and UTs have been advised through the sanction order
to ensure that at least 10% of the total expenditure of the State/UT for the current year is on quality
interventions as listed in Category II.
Further, all States and UTs have been given specific commitments focused on improvement in learning
outcomes during the finalization of their Annual Plans under SSA for 2016-17.
MHRD has developed a web portal called SSA SHAGUN (from the words Shaala and Gunvatta)
which has two parts i.e., one is a Repository of good practices, photographs, videos, studies, newspaper
articles etc on elementary education, State /UT wise. These are in the public domain. Its purpose is to
showcase success stories and also to provide a platform for all stakeholders to learn from each other. This
would also instill a positive competitive spirit among all the States and UTs.
The second part is regarding the online monitoring of the SSA implemented by States and UTs and can
be accessed by Government Officers at all levels using their specific passwords. It comprises questionnaires,
related to various interventions under SSA and the performance of the State, which will be filled in by the
States and UTs. There are 122 Reports which will be automatically generated from the data filled in the
questionnaires. These Reports, along with the success stories in the Repository, has created an online
platform to see the status of implementation of the SSA and the elementary education in all States and UTs.
MHRD, through NCERT, has developed Learning Outcomes for each class in Languages (Hindi,
English and Urdu), Mathematics, Environmental Studies, Science and Social Science up to the Elementary
stage. Care has been taken to develop the outcomes following consultations with States, UTs, SCERTs and
education experts from organizations including civil society organizations. The Learning Outcomes developed
by NCERT are based on the minimum levels of learning to facilitate the monitoring of students against
expected benchmarks.
These are being included in the Central Rules of the Right of Children to Free & Compulsory Education
(RTE) Act, 2009. A simplified version of these learning goals for display on the school notice board is being
finalized.
Recommendations/Observations
29.1 The Committee recommends that the Government of India should set the achievable goals and all
elements of education system viz., teachers’ training, on-sight support, materials and measurement, etc.,
have to be aligned to help schools and resultantly teachers help children learn better. Plans can be reviewed
and adjusted on year-to-year basis but the sustainable efforts have to be made for expanding the outreach
in the field of elementary education.
Action Taken
The RTE Act 2009 and National Curriculum Framework (NCF), 2005 both point to building on the
child’s knowledge, potential and talent through a child centric approach. It suggests that everything done in

5
or for the school should be geared towards a measurable development in student’s learning level and
prepares them for independence of thought and action, life-long learning, democratic values, creativity
and life skills.
The Central Government, through SSA, supports the State Governments and UT Administrations
on several interventions to improve teaching standards, including inter-alia;   regular in-service teachers’
training, induction training for newly recruited teachers, training of all untrained teachers to acquire
professional qualifications through Open Distance Learning (ODL) mode academic support for teachers
through block and cluster resource centres, training on ICT Component, Inclusive Education, Gender
Sensitization and Adolescent Education is provided. Under SSA, the focus is to give subject specific, need
based and relevant in service teacher training to both elementary and secondary teachers for their
professional develop ment.
The focus of the Department is to align all its efforts towards improvement in learning outcomes of
children at elementary stage.
Recommendations/Observations
34. The Department of School Education and Literacy in its background note has apprised the Committee
of the new initiatives taken up by Department in the field of elementary education under the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan (SSA) for improving the quality of education. The Committee admires these initiatives, like Swachha
Vidyalaya, Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB), Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (RAA), Shaala - Siddhi,
School Leadership Development Programme, Vidyanjali, Twinning programme (Partnership Between Schools)
and E- Pathshala. The Committee wishes the Department to excel in the field of all these eight initiatives
and expect to get the details of concrete measurable achievements made therein so far, from the department
so that a review can be made for the success rate, including constraints, if any, and overall responses.
Besides, by interactions with various stakeholders in the field of elementary education, the Committee
during its visit to select places, was impressed for setting up of Smart Classes in Govt. schools, which would
augment the quality of teaching–learning process of education for students.
Action Taken
The Department is supporting States and UTs to implement national level initiatives to improve the
quality of education.
i. The ‘Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat’ (PBBB), a sub-programme of the SSA, in classes I and II
focusing on foundational learning in early grades with an emphasis on reading, writing and
comprehension and Mathematics. States and UTs have been implementing specific interventions
like ABL in Tamil Nadu, Nalli Kali in Karnataka, Pragya in Gujarat; steps have been taken to
develop specific teacher training modules for teachers teaching students in classes 1 and 2.
Punjab, Meghalaya, Delhi have introduced programmes for strengthening teaching of maths in
classes 1 and 2; in Sikkim schools have set up reading corners for children in the foundational
classes through support from community members.
ii. The Rashtriya Aavishkar Abhiyan (RAA), also under the SSA, was launched by Late Dr. A.P.J.
Abdul Kalam. This aims to motivate and engage children of the age group 6-18 years, in Science,
Mathematics and Technology by observation, experimentation, inference drawing and model
building, through both inside and outside classroom activities. Schools have been adopted for

6
mentoring by Institutions of Higher Education like IIT’s, IISER’s and NIT’s. In some States
students have been taken for exposure visits to factories, research hubs; science and maths
clubs are being formed at the school levels, students are participating in competitions and
exhibitions to showcase their innovations in Maths, Science and Technology.
Comments of the Committee
The Committee notes the reply furnished by the Government.  However, the Department
should inform the Committee about the data on functional smart classes in Government Schools.
Recommendations/Observations
36. An overview of MDMS presented the genesis of this scheme and the Committee finds that Mid-Day
Meal in schools has had a long history in India. In 1925, a Mid-Day Meal Programme was introduced for
disadvantaged children in Madras Municipal Corporation. By the mid 1980s, three States viz. Gujarat,
Kerala and Tamil-Nadu and the UT of Pondicherry had universalized a cooked Mid-Day Meal Programme
with their own resources for children studying at the primary stage. By 1990-91, the number of States
implementing the Mid-Day Meal Programme with their own resources on a universal or a large scale basis
had gone up to twelve States. Considering the aspect of enhancing enrollment, retention and attendance and
simultaneously with a view to improve the nutritional level among the children, the National Programme of

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
Recommendations/Observations
30. The Committee, after having an in-depth analysis in the subject matter takes note of the educational
development in India, which is neither homogenous in regional spread nor neutral to social formations. It
has a strong bias in favour of economically developed areas with strong infrastructural support as compared
to the backward regions of the country. It is disheartening indeed that in spite of planned efforts, of course,
of Planning Commission/NITI AYOG, regional disparities in the field of quality based educational
development continue to be glaring. Germane to this, for the ongoing SSA mission, the Committee considers
decentralization as a major strategy for planning and management of elementary education. The
decentralization, within the national framework of SSA sounds paradoxical as every region of the country
counts on the diversity of culture, language, etc.
Action Taken
SSA envisages decentralized, need based and participatory planning in a bottom – up approach. All
States and UTs submit their proposal under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) Programme through their
Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B).  Based on their proposal, the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the
Ministry of Human Resource Development approves an outlay as per the programmatic and financial norms
of the scheme, which includes the share of both the centre and the states.
The RTE Act gives immense importance to School Management Committee as a part of decentralized
structure and one in which the parents will have a very significant role. Essential provisions regarding
constitution and functions of SMCs have been given in Sections 21 and 22. Section 21 of the Right of
Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE), 2009 stipulates that each Government school, Government
Aided school and school belonging to a specified category should have a School Management Committee
(SMC) mandated with the work to monitor the working of the school; prepare and recommend School
Development Plan; and monitor the utilisation of the grants received, besides their other activities. The SMC
is mandatory for all elementary schools.  Some Government schools also have Parent Teacher Associations
(PTAs) which perform similar functions as assigned to SMC. Under SSA, procurement of uniforms and
textbooks is also decentralized to the school level.
Comments of the Committee
The Committee feels that the empowerment of SMCs/PTAs and the increased role of parents
in the SMCs are steps taken in the right direction. Ministry’s reply does not categorically
states the steps being taken by them with regard to removing the regional imbalances that
Committee emphasized in its recommendation. Accordingly, the observations of the Committee
regarding the regional disparity in the educational development, which shows a huge negative
bias against the economically backward areas has not been addressed in the Department’s
response.
The regional imbalance in so far as the infrastructural development and quality based
educational development continues to be unaddressed. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Department should make more concerted efforts to bring about the infrastructural changes
10

11
and quality of education provided in the backward areas of the Country, where the options of school
children are limited unlike in the more developed regions of the Country.
Recommendations/Observations
30.1 The Committee recommends that government of India should bring out time bound programmes to
minimize the gap wherever States are standing differently in their educational status. This is the proven
pathway through which the SSA’ s time frame of universalisation of elementary Education in true sense, and
not for name sake, be realized. The Committee also recommends that this is the prime duty of the Government
of India not to obviate from the endeavor that if the SSA is an opportunity for States to develop their own
vision of elementary education, as the basic framework of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan’s claims, the States have
to fit themselves with the broader notional goal of providing useful and relevant elementary education for
all in the category of 6-14 years age group.
Action Taken
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 provides for free and
compulsory education for the children of the age of 6-14 years in neighbourhood schools till completion of
elementary education. The Department has issued various advisories and guidelines to the States and UTs
for effective implementation of various provisions of the RTE Act, 2009.
All States and UTs are implementing the RTE Act, 2009 as per their own State RTE Rules. The central
Government provides financial support to the States and UTs under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of SSA
for implementing the provisions of RTE Act, 2009.
Several new initiatives by the Department viz. Swachh Vidyalaya Abhiyan, Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat,
Rashtriya Aavishkar Abhiyan have been launched under the SSA scheme to guide the States and UTs in
providing useful and relevant elementary education for all children in the age group of 6-14 years.
Comments of the Committee
The Committee feels that in order to realize the objectives of the RTE Act, 2009, the States
need to effectively implement the various schemes/initiatives like Swachh Vidyalaya Abhiyan, Padhe
Bharat Badhe Bharat, Rashtriya Aavishkar Abhiyan etc.  The role of the Central Government is not
limited to the framing of the laws/guidelines but also to ensure that its objectives are achieved.
Hence, a robust monitoring mechanism need to be set up for checking the implementation in a
timely and qualitative manner, which is at present, not visible and more focus is required, especially
in the worst performing States/UTs.

Section 3(1) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 states:

BRCs/URCs and CRCs are the most critical units for providing training and on-site support to schools

Recommendations/Observations
35. The Committee notes the increased devolution of funds from 32% to 42% through 14th Finance
Commission Award, effective from 2015-16. The Committee shows its concern that States have not reported
earmarking funds exclusively for education out of the increased devolution of funds.
35.1 The Committee, therefore, recommends for inspiring States for the proportionate adjustment of increased
devolution of funds on education.
Action Taken (35 & 35.1)
Education is in the Concurrent List and the responsibility of running majority of the schools vests with
the States. SSA is the designated vehicle for implementation of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory
Education (RTE) Act, 2009. Section 7(1) of the RTE Act, 2009, states that both the Centre and the State
shall have concurrent responsibility for providing funds for carrying out the provisions of the Act.  Section
7(2) states that estimates for implementing the Act shall be prepared and the PAB outlay may be taken as the
estimates prepared in compliance with this sub-section.  Further, Section 7(3) states that the Central
Government shall provide to the State Government, as grants-in-aid of revenues, such percentage of
expenditure as it may determine, while, Section 7(5) states that the State Government shall, taking into
consideration the sums provided by the Central Government to a State Government, be responsible to
provide funds for the implementation of the provisions of the Act.  It is, therefore, clear that the responsibility
for meeting the fund requirement vests with both the Centre and the States.
With the acceptance of the recommendations of the 14th Finance Commission by the Government of
India, the devolution of funds to the States has been increased from 32% to 42 % of the net Union Tax
Receipts.  In this regard, it is stated that States have received an additional fund of ` 186149.79 crore more
during 2015-16 as compared to 2014-15 through 14th FC Award.  Similarly, there is additional devolution of
funds of ` 232528.13 crore more during 2016-17 as compared to 2014-15.  With the enhanced devolution
of funds, States have been advised to allocate more funds to SSA so as to carry out the functions and
responsibilities conferred upon the States by Section 7(5) of the RTE Act, 2009.   Accordingly, this Department
has written to the Chief Secretaries of all the States for ensuring the allocation of adequate amount of funds
for the School Education Sector in their state budget.
However, it is felt that these funds are untied and States may not be allocating enough funds towards
the education sector. It is, therefore, suggested that these funds need to be ring fenced so that at least 30%
of it can be used for social sector alone including education.

16
Comments of the Committee

fund allocations to State due to devolution of fund not being proportionately utilized for the education
Sector.  The Committee agrees with the suggestion of the Ministry for ring fencing of these funds
so as to ensure that atleast 30% can be used only for Social Sector including education.  The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry must seek ways and means to achieve this
objective and also inform the Committee of the action taken in this regard in its replies.

38. The Committee expresses its concern that most of the States did not follow the guidelines of Government

The MDM guidelines envisage that transport assistance is to be given for transportation of food grains
from nearest FCI godown to the School. But in hilly areas it is not possible to deliver the food grain up to

Since the gunny bags are filled FCI without weighing each bag,  these  gunny bag contains varying  quantity

adulteration and pilferage of food-grains owing to the long supply chain in the delivery of food-
grains to the schools.  The Committee re-iterates its recommendation that a foolproof mechanism
should be established to solve the problem of adulteration and pilferage and the first step in this
direction would be to eliminate middlemen/shorten the supply chain to the school.  Further, steps
should be taken to identify points of failure/improvements required, so that these can be corrected
at the earliest.

The Committee feels that the empowerment of SMCs/PTAs and the increased role of parents

bias against the economically backward areas has not been addressed in the Department’s
response. The regional imbalance in so far as the infrastructural development and quality based
educational development continues to be unaddressed. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Department should make more concerted efforts to bring about the infrastructural changes
and quality of education provided in the backward areas of the Country, where the options of school
children are limited unlike in the more developed regions of the Country. (Para 30)
The Committee feels that in order to realize the objectives of the RTE Act, 2009, the States
need to effectively implement the various schemes/initiatives like Swachh Vidyalaya Abhiyan, Padhe
Bharat Badhe Bharat, Rashtriya Aavishkar Abhiyan etc.  The role of the Central Government is not
limited to the framing of the laws/guidelines but also to ensure that its objectives are achieved.
Hence, a robust monitoring mechanism need to be set up for checking the implementation in a
timely and qualitative manner, which is at present, not visible and more focus is required, especially
in the worst performing States/UTs. (Para 30.1)
The Committee takes note of the reply. However, no tangible steps are visible.  The Committee,
